parties: Haapki Moms Private Limited (Peeko) [founder-led]; Chiratae Ventures (lead investor); Stellaris Venture Partners (existing investor); angel investors
headline: Peeko Series A closes at ₹67.4 crore led by Chiratae Ventures with angel participation for vertical quick-commerce babycare expansion.
sum: <cite index="1-1">Bengaluru-headquartered babycare platform Peeko has raised Rs 67.4 crore in a Series A round of funding led by Chiratae Ventures, with participation from existing investor Stellaris Venture Partners and prominent angel investors.</cite> <cite index="1-3">Peeko said it will use this funding towards business expansion, technology development, and hiring as it looks to deepen its presence in Bengaluru and expand into newer cities.</cite>
implication: Vertical quick-commerce in India now attracts institutional capital at scale (₹67 cr+ rounds) for specialist consumer categories; the try-and-buy model for baby products-structurally different from groceries-emerges as a defensive differentiation in commodity delivery markets.
detail: <cite index="1-5">Founded in 2025 by IIT alumni Chetan Sharma, Vivek Khetan, and Abhijit Gairola, Peeko aims to be the parenting partner for new-age parents who avoid buying baby apparel and toys online as it does not solve the problem of touch-and-feel, and delivery speed.</cite> <cite index="4-2">Filings show it went into the round priced at ₹186 crore, 55% above where its seed closed last September.</cite> <cite index="22-1">Currently operating three dark stores in Bengaluru and covering around 55% of the city, Peeko plans to double its network to six stores by the end of 2026.</cite> <cite index="1-8">By bringing an offline-like shopping experience to the doorstep, we've earned the trust of more than one lakh parents who have shopped on our platform since we launched eleven months ago.</cite>

framework.note: Private placement of equity shares to registered category investors (Chiratae, Stellaris, angels); board approval and filing mandatory.
Not directly triggered if no foreign investor participation; if present, requires RBI Schedule-1 Category II declaration for venture capital.
Shareholders' agreements, SAFE/KISMET notes (if used), investment documents form the core enforceable contracts.
No trigger on fundraise itself; Peeko's quick-commerce model (rapid delivery of baby products) subject to GST at point of sale and inter-state logistics.
Peeko's app-based platform must comply with data privacy, consumer protection disclaimers, and return-window mandates (14-day easy return rule).
Try-and-buy model creates explicit return-window liability; e-commerce seller obligations and dispute resolution forums apply.
If Chiratae deployed Fund IV, regulatory thresholds on illiquidity and investor eligibility apply; no direct trigger on investee, but structural precedent for VC gate-keeping.

structure.consideration: ₹67.4 crore ($7 million equivalent at ~₹96/$1 Aug 2026 rate)
conditions: Peeko registered as Haapki Moms Private Limited (28 May 2025)
Pre-Series A seed round: $3.2 million (Aug 2025) by Stellaris; final seed tranche ₹9 crore (May 2026) valued company at ₹186 crore post-money
Series A priced at ₹186 crore post-money (55% above seed close)
Equity dilution across co-founders (pre-Series A founder stake ~68%), Stellaris (~24%), ESOP pool (~5%)
Use of proceeds: geographic expansion (dark stores in Bengaluru, new cities), tech stack (parenting-partner platform, AI recommendations), hiring
approvals: Investment Committee approval (Chiratae Ventures Fund IV, Stellaris LPA)
MCA filing of share capital alteration (Form MGT-14, e-form INC-22A)
structure.novel: Structuring of equity round with try-and-buy consumer model as explicit growth lever; late-stage seed tranching (₹9 cr top-up in May 2026, 3 months pre-Series A) reflects market momentum; parenting-tech platform as post-commerce expansion vector (not typical quick-commerce thesis).

triggers.note: Board resolution, Board's Report on issuance, filing of shareholding pattern required with MCA.

triggers.law: Schedule I, FEMA Regulations (Category II VC definition)
triggers.note: If Chiratae/Stellaris deployed foreign capital, Series A counts as 'foreign investment' in Indian startup; RBI ECB or Liberalized Remittance Scheme (LRS) declaration if non-resident angels.
Peeko's app captures parental data (children's age, sizes, purchase history) triggering personal data protection; DISHA framework for e-commerce seller obligations.
Try-and-buy feature creates explicit product return liability within 14 days; NCLAT/District Consumer Commission jurisdiction if disputes.
